overview: The HC-12 aims for the sweet spot between the NRF24L01/LoRa's SPI complexity and Bluetooth's short range: it's a plain UART wireless serial link, meaning it plugs in and works almost exactly like the HC-05 Bluetooth module — bytes sent to one module's serial input come out the other module's serial output — but with roughly 100x the range (up to ~1km in open air) because it operates in the 433MHz band rather than 2.4GHz Bluetooth/WiFi. Configuration (channel, power, baud rate) is done through AT commands via a dedicated SET pin, and it has no pairing process at all — any two HC-12 modules on the same channel simply hear each other.
simpleSummary: A long-range wireless module that sends data like a walkie-talkie, reaching much farther than Bluetooth.

specifications.range: Up to ~1km line-of-sight (lower in practice with obstacles)
specifications.dataRate: Up to 100kbps (typically configured much lower to maximize range)

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.currentLimit: ~100 mA peak during transmission (higher power settings draw more)
pinMap.gotcha: At the highest transmit power setting, current draw can exceed what a microcontroller's onboard 5V regulator comfortably supplies alongside everything else.

pinMap.name: SET
pinMap.function: Pulling LOW puts the module into AT command configuration mode instead of normal transparent-serial mode.
pinMap.gotcha: Forgetting to pull this LOW before sending AT commands means the module just treats your configuration commands as data to transmit, silently failing to reconfigure.

useCases.title: Long-range remote control
useCases.scenario: Control a boat, car, or drone from much farther away than Bluetooth or NRF24L01 would allow.

useCases.title: Wireless sensor relay across a large property
useCases.scenario: Relay sensor data from a distant outbuilding back to a central receiver.

oftenConfusedWith: NRF24L01 (SPI interface, shorter range, higher data rate)
oftenUpgradedTo: LoRa modules for even longer range at the cost of a more complex SPI interface
